title: The event-loop invariant runsToGood_Invariant preserved by one machine step
intent: Name the event loop's invariant `runsToGood_Invariant` (the machine runs to a good-ready state and is valid) and prove it is preserved by one machine step, so that ToplevelLoop instantiates it for a concrete loop and thereby shows an infinite loop never reaches a bad state.

parent.name: runsToGood_is_Invariant
parent.statement:
Lemma runsToGood_is_Invariant: forall (st: RiscvMachineL),
      runsToGood_Invariant st -> mcomp_sat (run1 iset) st runsToGood_Invariant.

children.name: run1_get_sane
children.statement:
Lemma run1_get_sane: forall iset (P Q: RiscvMachineL -> Prop) mach,
      valid_machine mach ->
      mcomp_sat (run1 iset) mach P ->
      (forall mach': RiscvMachineL,
          (exists diff, mach'.(getLog) = diff ++ mach.(getLog)) ->
          valid_machine mach' ->
          P mach' ->
          Q mach') ->
      mcomp_sat (run1 iset) mach Q.
children.closed_by: pose proof run1_sane as A; unfold mcomp_sane in A; apply proj2 in A; eapply mcomp_sat_weaken
children.note: Project lemma in GoFlatToRiscv.v: attaches the sanity conclusions of run1_sane (valid_machine and a log prefix) to a run1 step.

children.name: runsTo_safe1_inv
children.statement:
Lemma runsTo_safe1_inv: forall (st: RiscvMachineL),
      runsTo (mcomp_sat (run1 iset)) st safe1 ->
      mcomp_sat (run1 iset) st (fun st' => runsTo (mcomp_sat (run1 iset)) st' safe1).
children.closed_by: destruct R (on the runsTo hypothesis); the done case by run_1_2 then eapply run_pong, the step case by eapply mcomp_sat_weaken
children.note: Project lemma in ForeverSafe.v: turns a `runsTo ... safe1` hypothesis into a one-step `mcomp_sat (run1 iset)` that lands back in `runsTo ... safe1`.

children.name: run_Jal0
children.note: Project lemma in RunInstruction.v: the per-instruction execution lemma for `Jal Register0 jimm20` (the loop's jump-back).

children.name: runsToDone
children.note: Constructor of the inductive `runsTo` relation, declared in the external riscv-coq library (imported as riscv.Utility.runsToNonDet / riscv.Platform.Run), not part of the bedrock2 source; the glue cites it to close the runsTo relation once the state satisfies the predicate.

applicability.goal_shape: A stepwise 'eventually reaches P' relation (here `runsTo (mcomp_sat (run1 iset))` over the metric RISC-V machine) where the goal is to show a predicate `I` is preserved by one transition `run1`.
applicability.use_when: the property to preserve has a natural one-step formulation (`runsToGood_Invariant` = runs-to-good and valid_machine); the per-instruction behaviour is already proved elsewhere (run_Jal0 and its siblings in RunInstruction.v); the invariant is a strengthening of the target (runs-to-good, not merely not-bad).
applicability.avoid_when: the invariant itself needs an induction over the loop body (then that induction is the real content); the one-step execution lemmas for the relevant instructions do not exist; the machine step cannot be expressed as a single `run1` transition.

consequences: The move isolates the loop argument into (a) the invariant predicate `runsToGood_Invariant`, (b) the one-step preservation lemma, and (c) per-case execution lemmas. Obligations it creates: the two cases of a step must be distinguished (loop body vs jump-back, via the `done` flag and `goodReadyState_checks_PC`), and the preservation proof must discharge `valid_machine` on both the step and the stop (`run1_get_sane` and `runsToDone`). Failure modes: an invariant too weak to be preserved (the proof gets stuck at `goodReadyState_preserved_by_jump_back`), or a step lemma whose side conditions (jimm20 mod 4 = 0, footprint subset) the glue cannot discharge.
